title: Implement UUencode CTE decoding (x-uuencode, x-uue, uuencode)
description:
UUencode appears in real email as CTE: x-uuencode (also x-uue, uuencode). RFC 2045 permits x-token values; these three are conventional spellings. mail-parser returns Encoding::None and raw bytes for all of them; mime-tree must decode.

Changes:
1. Add TransferEncoding::UUEncode variant in part.rs.
2. In map_encoding() add arms for x-uuencode / x-uue / uuencode (case-insensitive) before the wildcard.
3. In decode_body_value() add a UUEncode arm: scan for begin NNN filename line, decode each subsequent line (first byte = line length, each char = (c - 32) and 0x3F), stop at backtick-only line or end line. Respect max_bytes. Set is_encoding_problem on malformed input and return partial decode. No charset conversion on decoded bytes.
4. Do not extract the UU begin-line filename; callers use ParsedPart.filename from MIME headers.
5. No external crate; implement from scratch.

Test oracle: Python uu module or UNIX uuencode utility. Example: python3 -c 'import uu, io; ...' or echo hello | uuencode hello.txt. Tests must NOT derive expected values from this crate.

Acceptance criteria:
- x-uuencode / x-uue / uuencode all map to TransferEncoding::UUEncode
- Well-formed UU body decodes to correct bytes (verified against Python/UNIX oracle)
- max_bytes respected
- Malformed input sets is_encoding_problem, returns partial decode
- Content before begin line skipped cleanly
